done.why: A few minutes of walking gave me nothing to do. The sword wouldn't move, and I only found scenery and a few objects I had no use for. Nothing pulled me on.

about: A classic Zork-style underground dungeon. You arrive at the bottom of a stair as someone who has passed earlier tests and now face a final one. You explore caves, a cliff and a shore with a lantern.

moments.note: Moving south into the dark gave a grue warning right away. It was a fun classic nod.
The Elvish sword in the rock can't be taken, and there is no hint about how. It's a dead end for now.
The sunlit cliff with giant trees was a vivid spot. It also hinted at a hidden something among the trees, plus a rope and bread.
I reached a beach with quicksand and mist but had no goal or direction. I lost interest.

wished: A clear sense of what to do next, or some early puzzle or hook.
Some way to interact with the thing hiding among the trees, since I skipped it.

lines.line: A few seedlings from the world above, nurtured by the sunlight and occasional rains, have grown into giant trees, making this a virtual oasis in the desert of the Underground Empire.
lines.why: This was the best image in the game, and it made the place feel real.

fun.why: Only wandering, with no payoff within a few minutes.

engagement.why: I had no goal, so I quit quickly.

difficulty.why: I had no direction, and the first obstacle, the sword, gave no hint. I couldn't tell how hard it really was.

interestingness.why: The dream intro and the setting were intriguing. The cliff with the hidden figure promised more.

prose.why: The room descriptions were evocative and well written.
